correctness.rationale: The exact fort equivalence requires delta(A) contained in B and deg_B(v)≠1 at every unselected original vertex. Minimality forces pure-edge cycles or, when originals are selected, a forest with selected-original support of n-1 or n; direct arguments prove sufficiency. The standard finite-graph fort-hitting equivalence then turns cycle constraints into forest complements and leaves exactly n forbidden one-vertex/star pairs. Cayley gives the minimum multiplicity. An executable independent-definition exhaustive checker confirms exact families and all polynomial coefficients for n=3,4,5; finite tests are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Minimal forts give the complete obstruction family for zero forcing. The theorem identifies all such obstructions for a natural infinite dense-graph subdivision, translates forcing into labeled spanning-forest complements with one precise obstruction, and determines an entire coefficient distribution and \(n(n^{n-2}-1)\) minimum solutions. These statements are structurally stronger than the known zero-forcing number and give reusable incidence-graph/graphic-matroid insight rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
